checks.source: MEAS: item db metadata read (collection 78rpm_charm; label Decca; matrix AR_8463-2; catalogue 1153); cached MP3 MD5 dd3569543aab… equals the Archive manifest; 260.58 s. The movement is complete (strings from about 2 s; horn’s hand-stopped G–A♭ slide to about 258 s). Pitch: the horn’s sustained F5 at 82–86 s measures 698–703 Hz and the second at about 226–231 s 700–705 Hz, within +0 to +5 cents of A = 440, so no speed or transposition issue. Horn in F: sounding F5 = written top C, E5 = written B, as the notes say.
checks.identity: EXT: Stuart, Complete Decca Classical Discography (Archive full text), session 0288: 25 May 1944, West Hampstead Studios; three sides (8461/64/66) re-made 8 Oct 1944; Pears, Brain, Boyd Neel String Orchestra, Britten; AR8461-66; (Nov45) (A)K1151-53. CHARM METS_AK_1151 read: disc 3 (cat. 1153) = AR_8463-2 (Elegy) and AR_8464-4 (Dirge); the set is autocoupled 1+6, 2+5, 3+4. Session date 25 May 1944 is an inference (8463 not among the re-made sides); the dossier says so.
checks.notes: EXT: Cooke blog text (HTML raw) confirms the long introduction and conclusion, worm in the strings, exposed top C in the 15th slow bar slipping a semitone, recitative, weighty double-bass pizzicato. Clarke (Seen and Heard, 11 Apr 2024): two sustained high Cs resolving to B natural; tenor against shifting chords. Sackville-West quotation, Sun Valley note and Wikipedia (advice on the poems; dedication) verified. Boosey and Hawkes page: the two centrepiece settings. Gramophone Dec 1945 review independently says the horn solo is repeated after the tenor. MEAS: first C–B at 82 s (F5 to about 86.5 s, then E5 to about 94.5 s); quiet gap 95–101 s; voice-band energy 105–150 s; second C–B at about 225.5–237 s; section 101 and cue times fit. Six notes for 260.6 s (limit 7). Voice rules checked. Not an aural review.
